transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, yeah, thank you for fitting me in. I just... I really didn't know what else to do because I came in today because my mind is just... it's constantly jumping all over the place, and I absolutely cannot turn it off. 

Like, I work in a materials science lab right now, and we just got this new corporate partnership, which I guess should be a good thing for funding, but my brain is just completely fixated on whether they're going to cut my position to streamline things. Because I only have some college so far, I don't have my full degree yet, so I feel like I'm totally expendable to them. And then, if I'm not worrying about getting laid off, my mind immediately jumps to agonizing over my actual bench work and whether my data are wrong—like, did I contaminate a batch, did I record a metric wrong, is the PI going to look at my spreadsheets and realize I messed up months of research? 

And then it just keeps going. Like, if I get fired or my data is bad, my bills are just going to completely pile up, and I'm already stressing about how expensive everything is. And I already know my family thinks I'm falling behind everyone else my age because I'm 24 and still just a tech trying to figure things out, and it just spirals into this huge, overwhelming panic about whether I've already completely ruined my chances at ever getting into grad school. It's just this endless loop every single day... the lab partnership, the bills, my family judging me, grad school, my data... it just never, ever stops.
Have you been avoiding any situations or activities because of these worries?

Avoiding? Um... no. No, I don't think so. I mean, honestly, I wish I could just hide under the covers sometimes and avoid it all, but I still do everything. I still go into the lab every single morning. I get there at 7:30 AM on the dot, even though I usually sit in my car in the parking lot for, like, ten or fifteen minutes just gripping the steering wheel, running through every single possible thing that could go wrong with my bench work that day. But I still go inside. I still do the data entry, even though I'm agonizing over every single cell in the spreadsheet because I'm so scared of the new corporate guys seeing a mistake. 

And I definitely don't avoid my family, even though every time my mom calls, my stomach just completely drops because I know she's going to ask about when I'm going back to finish my degree and compare me to my cousins. I still pick up the phone. I just brace myself for it. I kind of feel like I don't really have the luxury to avoid things, you know? Because if I avoid work, then I actually *will* get fired, and then the bills really *will* pile up, which is exactly what I'm already so terrified of. So avoiding things would just make the whole spiral even worse, if that makes sense. 

So, yeah, I haven't stopped doing my normal routine or skipping out on activities or anything like that. It's just that actually *doing* the routine is completely exhausting because my brain is just screaming at me the entire time I'm doing it. I'm there, I'm doing the work, I'm talking to people... I'm just completely dreading every second of it. So... no, not avoiding, just... enduring it, I guess.
Have you been feeling sad or hopeless most of the time?

Sad or hopeless? Um... no, not really sad. I mean, I wouldn't say I'm walking around crying or feeling like there's no point to anything, you know? It's not like that heavy, dark feeling where you just can't get out of bed because you don't care anymore. I care *too* much. That's the whole problem. I care so intensely about every single little detail that it just burns me out. 

Like, when I'm sitting there looking at my spreadsheets, I'm not thinking, "Oh, what's the point, none of this matters." I'm thinking, "Oh my god, if this one decimal point is wrong, the entire project is ruined, the corporate guys will notice, my PI will hate me, and my life is over." It's this high-voltage, buzzing energy all the time. It's not sadness. It's just sheer terror that I'm going to mess up.

And hopeless? I don't know if hopeless is the right word either. Because I do have hope that I can fix things or keep things from falling apart, but it requires me to be on high alert 24/7. Like, I feel like if I just worry enough, if I just plan for every single disaster scenario, maybe I can prevent it. So I don't feel hopeless, I just feel like I'm constantly running on a treadmill that's going way too fast, and if I stop for even a second to catch my breath, I'm going to get thrown off and smash into the wall. So, no, not sad or hopeless. Just... completely, utterly frantic and exhausted from being so frantic all the time. It's like my brain is stuck in overdrive and the brakes are completely shot.
Have you been experiencing any physical symptoms like headaches or stomach problems?

Physical symptoms? Yeah, actually, um... yes. I mean, my stomach is usually in knots, but the main thing, the thing that's really bothering me physically, is just how incredibly tight my muscles are all the time. Especially my shoulders and my neck. They just stay so tight during the day, like they're locked up. 

I actually catch myself doing it, too. Like, I'll be sitting at my bench, or usually when I'm staring at those spreadsheets trying to make sure the corporate guys won't find a mistake, and I'll realize that my shoulders are practically hiked up to my ears. And my jaw! I clench my jaw so hard when I'm looking at the data. I don't even realize I'm doing it until my teeth start to ache, and then I try to relax it, but five minutes later, I'm right back to clenching it again because I'm just so stressed about missing a decimal point. 

And because of all that tension, by the time the evening rolls around, I get these awful headaches. They just sort of radiate up from my neck into the base of my skull. And my whole upper body just feels completely stiff and sore, honestly, like I've been physically hauling heavy lab equipment around all day, even though I've just been sitting at a desk or standing at a bench. It's just... it's like my body is physically bracing for an impact that never actually comes, all day long. So by the time I get home, I'm just aching and stiff, and my head is pounding from all the clenching and the tightness. It's really uncomfortable, and it just makes it even harder to try and relax when I finally do leave the lab, because my body is still physically stuck in that tense, wound-up state.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body, watching yourself go through your daily routine?

Outside of my body? Like... like watching myself? Um, no. No, I don't think I've ever felt anything like that. I mean, I'm definitely always right there in my body, mostly because my body is so uncomfortable and tense all the time, like I was just saying with the neck and the jaw clenching. It's kind of hard to feel disconnected from your body when it's screaming at you with a headache, you know? 

I mean, sometimes when I'm really, really spiraling about the spreadsheets and the corporate guys, or when I'm sitting in my car in the morning gripping the steering wheel, my mind is definitely somewhere else. Like, my mind is in the future, running through all the disaster scenarios, picturing getting fired, picturing the bills piling up, picturing my mom being disappointed. So my thoughts are definitely not in the present moment, but I don't feel like I'm physically floating above myself or watching myself like a movie or anything weird like that. I'm very much stuck inside my own head, and my head is very much attached to my body. 

It's actually kind of the opposite, I think. I feel too trapped in my body and too trapped in my thoughts. I wish I could step outside of myself sometimes just to get a break from the constant buzzing and the worrying, but no, I'm always just... me. Just sitting there, agonizing over the decimal points, feeling my shoulders hike up to my ears. So, yeah, no out-of-body experiences or anything. Just the regular, exhausting, everyday panicking.
Do you ever feel numb or detached from your emotions or the world around you?

Numb? Um... no. God, no, I really don't. Honestly, I kind of wish I did feel numb sometimes, because that sounds like an absolute vacation compared to what I'm actually dealing with. I feel the exact opposite of detached. It's like... it's like every single emotion and every single nerve ending I have is just dialed up to a hundred and fifty percent, all the time. 

If I were numb, I wouldn't care so much about the spreadsheets or the data. I'd just sit at my lab bench, run my samples, and go home, you know? Like, if my PI walks past my bench and just has a slightly weird look on his face, or if he doesn't say good morning in the exact same tone he usually does, I don't feel detached from that. I feel this massive, sharp spike of panic right in the middle of my chest. I absorb everything around me. I'm hyper-aware of the world, actually. I hear the hum of the fume hoods, I hear the fluorescent lights buzzing, I hear the corporate guys walking down the hall, and every single little thing feels like this huge, pressing threat that I have to react to. 

So I'm definitely not detached. I'm way too attached to everything. I care so much about every tiny little interaction and every possible mistake that I just can't turn it off. People are always telling me to just tune things out, but how do you tune it out when your brain is screaming at you that everything is a catastrophe? Like, I'll go home at the end of the day, and I'm still feeling the raw stress from a ten-second conversation I had at nine in the morning about polymer stress-testing. I just replay it and replay it, feeling all that same anxiety all over again. So, no, definitely not numb. I feel everything, constantly, all the time, and it's just... I can't escape it. I really can't. I'm just always completely plugged in and short-circuiting.
How long have you been experiencing these overwhelming worries and physical symptoms?

Seven months. Yeah, it's been about seven months of just... this. This constant, grinding state of panic. I know exactly when it started, too, because it wasn't always this bad. I mean, I've always been a little high-strung, you know, you kind of have to be to work in a lab, you have to care about the details. But this whole thing where I can't breathe and my jaw is killing me and I'm convinced I'm going to ruin my entire life over a decimal point? That started exactly seven months ago. 

That was when the lab got this huge funding shift. We entered into this massive commercial partnership, and suddenly everything changed. Before that, it was just pure research, you know? We were just trying to understand the materials, doing good science. But then these corporate guys came in, and suddenly it wasn't just about the science anymore. It was about deliverables, and profit margins, and meeting these insane, arbitrary deadlines they set without even understanding the chemistry involved. 

They changed how everything was being run, from the top down. Suddenly, every single sample I ran wasn't just a data point, it was a potential multimillion-dollar mistake. If I messed up a polymer batch, it wasn't just "oh well, let's try again tomorrow and see what went wrong," it was "you're delaying the product launch and costing the company a fortune." The pressure just skyrocketed overnight. 

And my PI, he completely changed, too. He used to be so laid back, but once the commercial money came in, he started micromanaging everything, breathing down my neck, constantly asking for updates before the reactions were even finished. And that's when I really started feeling it. The tight shoulders, the headaches, the spiraling thoughts in the car every morning. It just flipped like a switch seven months ago when those corporate suits walked into our lab and turned my job into this high-stakes nightmare. I haven't had a single day of peace since they showed up. Not one. I just wake up dreading going in, and I go to sleep dreading waking up to go in. Seven months of just pure, unadulterated stress.
Have you ever had a period of more than a few months where you didn't feel this level of anxiety?

I mean, it really depends on how you define "this level," I guess. Because... well, like I was saying, the really intense stuff, the feeling like my chest is going to cave in and the corporate guys are going to fire me and ruin my life, that’s just been the last seven months. But before that... I don't know, I'm trying to think if I was ever actually, like, relaxed. Because even before the commercial partnership, when we were just doing the pure research and my PI was chill, I was still... I was still me, you know? 

I was still double-checking my lab notebook four or five times before I went home. I was still lying awake at night thinking about whether I might have accidentally contaminated a sample because I brushed my glove against the edge of the fume hood. It’s just that back then, the stakes felt different. It was just about getting the science right, not about losing millions of dollars for some shareholders. But was I calm? Was I just coasting? No. I don't think I've ever really had a period of a few months where I was just completely fine and not worrying about something. 

Even back when I was taking classes, before I paused school to just work full-time in the lab... I was constantly, constantly stressed about my coursework. I’d be up until three in the morning agonizing over organic chemistry mechanisms, totally convinced I was going to fail and that my mom would be devastated and that I'd never get a job. I was always on edge. I was always waiting for the other shoe to drop, even when things were technically going fine. 

So, if you're asking if I've had a period without *this* specific, paralyzing, seven-months-of-hell level of terror? Yeah, I guess before the buyout, it wasn't quite this extreme. But a period of a few months without feeling that buzzing in my head? Without feeling like I have to perfectly control every single variable in my life or else everything falls apart? I honestly... I don't think so. I really don't. I can't remember a time where I just felt okay for months on end. It’s always been something. If it wasn't the corporate guys, it was my PI. If it wasn't the PI, it was my grades. It's like my brain always has to find a problem to latch onto and just squeeze the life out of it. I guess... I guess the volume just got turned up from an eight to a ten when the commercial funding came in, but the radio has definitely always been playing, if that makes sense. I just don't know how to turn it off.
Have you ever had a time in your life when you felt anxious or worried about almost everything, even when there weren't any major stressors or changes happening?

Almost everything? Yeah. God, yeah. That's... honestly, that's exactly why I finally made the appointment to come in here. Because it's not just the corporate buyout thing, even though that's the loudest thing right now. It's like my brain can't just pick one single thing to freak out about, it has to be *everything* all at once, no matter what's actually happening in reality. 

Like, my mind is just constantly, constantly jumping around. I'll be sitting there, maybe it's a Sunday morning and absolutely nothing is going on, totally quiet, but my brain is just spiraling. First I'm terrified about whether our lab's new partnership is going to end up cutting my position entirely, because you know how these corporate things go, they always downsize the junior techs first to save a buck. But then, before I can even fully process that thought, I'm suddenly obsessing over whether my data from yesterday's polymer batch are wrong, and if I need to go back and rerun the whole assay or if I'm going to look like an idiot in front of the PI. 

And then, somehow, that jumps right into this sheer panic about money. I start convincing myself my bills are going to pile up and I won't be able to pay rent or afford groceries if I get fired over the data. And then—and it just keeps going, it literally never stops—I start thinking about my parents, and I get this horrible, heavy sinking feeling that my family thinks I'm completely falling behind in life because I paused my degree to work full-time in this lab. They never say it, but I just know they're thinking it. Which leads me right into obsessing over whether I've already completely ruined my chances at grad school. Like, maybe I've been out of classes too long, maybe my transcripts aren't competitive enough anymore, maybe I've just totally wrecked my entire future before I even hit twenty-five. 

It's just this endless, exhausting loop. Work, data, bills, family, grad school, over and over and over again. It doesn't even matter if nothing bad has happened that day. My brain just runs this marathon of worst-case scenarios about literally every single aspect of my life, and I can't break out of it.
Have you experienced excessive worry about a variety of things for more than six months?

Yeah, exactly. I mean, like I was saying earlier, it's been right around seven months now of this really intense, non-stop worrying about... well, about all those different things I just listed. 

It all tracks back to that exact timeline I was talking about, when the lab went through that massive funding shift. That commercial partnership coming in and just completely changing how everything was being run from the ground up... that was exactly seven months ago. And that's really when the floodgates opened on all of this. I know I already talked your ear off about the corporate buyout and the new management, but it's just so clearly the dividing line for me. 

Like, sure, I've always been a bit high-strung, but this specific thing? Where I'm simultaneously obsessing over my bills, and my parents' hidden disappointment, and the polymer data, and my grad school transcripts all at the exact same time, every single day? That's been going on for seven solid months. I can literally look back at my calendar and point to the week the new corporate guys took over the lab, because that was the very last time I remember not feeling like my brain was juggling a dozen different worst-case scenarios at once. So, yeah, to answer your question, it's definitely been more than six months. Seven months of just... this.
Do you find it hard to stop worrying once you start?

Oh, absolutely. It's... it's honestly impossible. Once the train leaves the station, there are just no brakes at all. 

I'll be at work, right? And I'll literally try to bargain with my own brain. I'll sit down at my desk and I'll try to tell myself to just focus on one single task. Just... just finish this one progress report for the new management guys, or just focus on checking this one polymer assay. Just put your head down, do the chemistry, and block everything else out. That's what I tell myself. 

But it never works. Because I'll be looking at the assay data, and then I'll think, 'Wait, did I calibrate the equipment perfectly this morning?' And that one little worry just... it immediately sets off another one. It's like dominoes. I'll think, 'If I didn't calibrate it right, the data is slightly off. If the data is off, the report is wrong. If the report is wrong, the corporate guys are going to think I'm incompetent and fire me.' 

One worry sets off another, and another, and another, and pretty soon I'm not even working anymore. I'm just sitting there, completely frozen, staring at the screen while my head is running through every possible way things could go wrong. And I'll sit there for twenty, thirty minutes, just completely paralyzed by it. I know I need to stop, I know I need to just type the next sentence of the report or run the next sample, but I physically can't make my brain shift gears. It's like I'm trapped in this horrible simulation of my own life falling apart, and I can't find the exit button. Even if I try to get up and walk to the breakroom to get a coffee just to snap out of it, the thoughts just follow me down the hallway. I just... I can't shut it off once it starts.
Has your worrying been interfering with your ability to function at work or in your personal relationships?

Yeah, it really is. It’s... honestly, it’s getting to the point where I feel like I’m just dropping the ball on literally everything in my life right now. 

Like, just the other week at the lab, I actually completely missed an internal deadline, which is so unlike me, I swear. I've always been the guy who has his stuff together. But I was supposed to turn in this synthesis summary, and I just... I couldn't do it. I was sitting there at my desk, looking at all the numbers, and I just couldn't organize my writing or get through the data review. My brain was just so clouded with all the other stuff I was worrying about, all those worst-case scenarios, that I couldn't string two coherent sentences together about the chemistry. I just kept moving paragraphs around and staring at the screen until the deadline blew right past me. And now, because of that, even just the super basic, routine responsibilities at work, like preparing the standard weekly reports for the new management, it all just feels like way too much to keep up with. I dread it. I sit down to do a routine report and I just feel completely overwhelmed.

And it’s definitely spilling over into my personal life, too, which really sucks because I need an outlet, but I just don't have the energy for it. I have this group of friends, and we usually do these art nights. Just a casual thing, you know, hanging out, drawing, trying to decompress and not think about work. But lately, I haven't even been showing up. The thought of just getting in my car and going there and trying to make small talk and act normal while my brain is spiraling... I just can't do it. I skip them. 

And even at home, it's bad. I usually try to help out by cooking for my family, since, you know, I'm living at home right now with the whole paused degree situation, and it used to be a nice way to contribute and show them I'm still trying. But lately? Even just the thought of figuring out a recipe and standing in the kitchen and cooking for them feels like this massive, impossible chore. It’s like every single normal, everyday thing, whether it's work or my friends or my family, is just entirely too much for me to handle right now. I just can't keep up with any of it anymore.
Do you feel like your worrying is causing you a lot of distress?

Oh, God, yes. So much distress. It's... it's honestly exhausting. It's like this heavy, suffocating blanket that I just can't take off, no matter how hot it gets or how much I'm struggling to breathe underneath it. 

I wake up in the morning, and before I even open my eyes, before I even consciously realize I'm awake, my stomach is already in knots. It's this physical ache, this tightness right in the center of my chest, like someone is sitting on me. And the emotional toll... I mean, I just feel so drained. I feel like I'm constantly on the verge of tears, or like I'm about to scream, but I can't do either because I'm just so completely depleted from the sheer effort of trying to keep it all together. 

I used to be a pretty easygoing guy, you know? I could laugh things off. If an experiment failed, or if I got a bad grade, I'd just shrug and say, 'Well, back to the drawing board.' But now? Now, every little thing feels like a life-or-death crisis. I feel so fragile, like I'm made of glass and the slightest tap is going to shatter me into a million pieces. And the worst part is, I know it's irrational. I know my parents aren't secretly plotting to kick me out, I know the corporate guys aren't monitoring my every keystroke, but knowing it doesn't stop the feeling. 

It's just this constant, low-level panic that spikes into sheer terror at the drop of a hat. I'll just be sitting in my car in the driveway, gripping the steering wheel until my knuckles are white, just crying because I'm so overwhelmed by everything and nothing all at once. I hate feeling like this. I hate who I've become. I just want to feel normal again, to not have every single waking moment be this agonizing struggle against my own thoughts. So, yeah, 'distress' is probably the best word for it, but honestly, it feels like an understatement. It's just... it's ruining me.
Is your worrying mostly about one area of your life, like work, or is it spread across many different areas?

It's literally everything. I mean, I wish it was just work, because then maybe I could leave it at the lab, right? Just clock out and be done. But it's not. I actually came in to see you specifically because my mind is just... it's constantly jumping from one catastrophe to the next, across every single part of my life. 

Like, okay, work is a big one. We have this new partnership at the lab with those new management guys I mentioned, and all I can think about is whether this partnership means they're going to restructure and just cut my position entirely. And then, even if they don't cut my position, I start obsessing over whether my data is wrong and they'll just fire me for being bad at my job anyway. 

But then the second I think about losing my job, my brain immediately jumps to money. I start panicking about how my bills are going to pile up, and I'll literally sit there doing the math in my head about how fast I'd burn through my tiny amount of savings paying for my car and my phone and just basic survival. 

And of course, thinking about not being able to support myself just brings it right back to my living situation. Since I'm living at home right now, I am constantly agonizing over what my parents are thinking. I just know my family thinks I'm falling behind everyone else my age. I'm 24, I should be out on my own, but instead I'm under their roof with this paused degree situation. Which then just triggers this whole other spiral about my future, because I was supposed to go get my master's or my PhD, and now I just lie awake at night entirely convinced that I've already completely ruined my chances at grad school. Like, what admissions committee is going to want a guy who couldn't even finish his undergrad in one straight shot and is just stuck running routine assays? 

So, yeah, it's definitely not just one area. It's the lab, it's the bills, it's my family, it's grad school... it just loops and loops through all of them. It's like my brain can't decide which part of my life is falling apart the fastest, so it just cycles through all of them on repeat.
Are you finding it difficult to maintain relationships with friends and family due to your worrying?

Yeah, I mean, like I was touching on a little bit earlier... it really is. It’s making it so incredibly hard to just be a normal son or a normal friend right now. 

I know I mentioned those art nights with my friends and how I've just stopped showing up, but it's... it's really starting to cause a rift. They text me, you know? They ask where I am, if I'm okay, if they did something wrong, and I just sit there and stare at my phone because I don't even know how to explain to them that I just can't do it. I feel like a terrible friend. But how do I tell them that I can't even handle my basic, everyday life right now? Like, I told you about how I completely blew past that internal lab deadline the other week because I literally couldn't organize my writing or get through a simple data review. When you're failing at things like that, things that used to be so easy, you just have absolutely zero emotional energy left for anyone else. 

And because of that, even just thinking about those routine weekly reports I have to prepare for work makes me so on edge that by the time I get home, I'm just... I'm useless. I'm completely useless to my family. I brought up the cooking thing before, how I used to make dinner for my parents to, I don't know, try to say thank you for letting me live at home while my degree is on pause. It used to be our time to talk and connect and maintain that relationship. But now? I walk in the door and the idea of just standing in the kitchen, chopping vegetables, trying to hold a normal conversation with my mom about her day without having a meltdown... it feels like climbing a mountain. I can't do it. I just go straight to my room and shut the door. 

So, yeah, I'm definitely pulling away from everyone. I just can't keep up with any of it anymore—not my friends, not my family, not my work... it’s all just slipping through my fingers because my brain is just too exhausted from worrying all day to actually be present with the people I care about.
Are there any areas of your life where you feel like your worrying is holding you back or causing problems?

Yeah, I mean, honestly, it's exactly what I was just saying. It's... it's holding me back in pretty much every single aspect of my day-to-day life. 

Like I mentioned a second ago with work, I completely missed that internal lab deadline. And it wasn't because I forgot about it or because I was being lazy. I was sitting right there at my desk, staring at the monitor, and I just... I literally couldn't organize my writing. The data review part of it, which should be the easiest thing in the world for me—I mean, reviewing data is my bread and butter in the lab—but it all just blurred together. I couldn't make sense of it, couldn't structure my thoughts, because my brain was just screaming at me about a million other things that could go wrong. 

And because I'm failing at the big things, now even the most basic, routine responsibilities just feel like they're a thousand pounds heavy. Like preparing those standard weekly reports... it takes me hours longer than it used to because I'm just paralyzed, second-guessing every single word I type. 

And it's bleeding into my personal life, too, like I was saying. Showing up for those art nights with my friends? I just can't do it. The idea of sitting there and trying to be creative and social while my chest is tight and my stomach is in knots... it's too much. And the cooking... man, I used to really enjoy cooking dinner for my family. It was a nice way to decompress and, you know, actually contribute to the household. But now, even just the thought of figuring out a recipe, getting the ingredients out, and standing in the kitchen feels like... I don't know, it just feels like way too much to keep up with. I can't even manage the bare minimum of my own life anymore. I'm just completely stalled out, everywhere I look.
Have you noticed any consistent patterns in how your worrying affects your relationships or daily activities over the past few months?

Patterns... well, I mean, the biggest pattern is really just the timeline of it all, honestly. Like, how long this has been dragging me down and just getting progressively worse. I can actually trace it back pretty specifically to about seven months ago. Yeah, it's been going on for seven solid months now. 

I know exactly when it started because that was when our lab had this massive funding shift. I think I mentioned those new management guys earlier? Well, we entered into this big commercial partnership, and it just... it completely changed how everything was being run. Almost overnight, it felt like. Before that, I was managing okay, you know? I was going in, doing my assays, I was hanging out with my friends at those art nights, I was cooking dinner for my parents. Things were normal. But when that funding shifted and the commercial guys came in and started changing all our procedures and expectations, looking over our shoulders, talking about deliverables and restructuring... that was the catalyst. 

So for the last seven months, the pattern has just been this slow, agonizing bleed of that initial work panic into literally every other corner of my life. It started with me just bringing the worry home from the lab, maybe losing a little sleep over the new protocols. But then, over these months, it just kept snowballing until it turned into not being able to text my friends back, and not being able to stand in the kitchen, and panicking about grad school and my savings. It's like that commercial partnership flipped a switch in my brain seven months ago, and I just haven't been able to turn it off since. Every week just compounds on the last one.
Are there any areas of your life where you feel like your worrying is causing you significant problems or impairment?

Yeah, I mean... I feel like I'm repeating myself a bit, but yes, absolutely. It's causing massive problems everywhere. I mean, it's just completely derailed me. 

Like I was saying about work, I completely blew past that internal lab deadline. And it wasn't just a small oversight, it was a major thing. I was sitting there, staring at my screen, and I just could not, for the life of me, organize my writing or get through the data review. It was like my brain was full of static. And because of that, now even the small things, the routine responsibilities that I used to do on autopilot, they feel impossible. Like preparing those weekly reports... it takes everything out of me. 

And it's not just work, it's my whole life. I mentioned the art nights with my friends... I just can't show up for them anymore. The thought of trying to be social and creative when I'm this wound up... I can't do it. And cooking for my family, which used to be my way of contributing and relaxing, it just feels like this insurmountable task. Getting the ingredients, following a recipe, standing in the kitchen... it's all just too much to keep up with. I feel like I'm failing at literally everything, big and small. Every single area of my life is just... it's just falling apart because I can't stop worrying long enough to actually function.
Do you feel like your worrying is significantly interfering with your ability to function in your daily life or maintain your relationships?

I know I keep saying the same things, but yes, it is. It really, really is. It’s like... it’s like my whole life is just slipping through my fingers, you know? I’m completely paralyzed by it. 

I mean, I was just talking about work, right? That internal lab deadline I missed? That wasn't just a one-off thing, that was a huge deal.
